plain: Genuine and proved to be real.

webster.text: Having a genuine original or authority, in opposition to that which is false, fictitious, or counterfeit; being what it purports to be; genuine; true; applied to things; as an authentic paper or register.

example.quote: What was the precise nature or extent of this proposition, or what the reasons for refusing it, is not ascertained by any authentic document, or even by accurate recollection.
example.cite: Alexander Hamilton, Opinion as to the Constitutionality of the Bank of the United States, Feb. 23, 1791
